bullets.title: GOOGL/MSFT/AMZN: Hyperscaler earnings tonight — AI capex scrutiny, cloud beat expected
bullets.body: MSFT Azure expected ~47% YoY growth (2pt beat) and GOOGL Cloud expected +105-115% YoY vs Street +90%, partly driven by TPU sales estimated at $5-7B in Q3. OpenAI announcing plans to buy Google TPUs diversifies away from pure NVDA reliance — bullish read-through for GOOGL. AMZN AWS expected +40% YoY; 2027 capex for all three hyperscalers modeled at $213-329B each, with debt financing rising from 9% to 32% of capex over last 12 months.

bullets.title: VRT: +16.5% premarket on monster Q3 beat; Americas organic +66%, orders +100%
bullets.body: Vertiv Q3 revenue $4.31B crushed FactSet consensus of $3.75B; FY guidance raised to $14.45-14.85B. Americas organic growth accelerated to 66% and orders grew 100% YoY. Sympathy moves: MOD +7%, FPS +6.5%.

bullets.title: STX: Beat Q1, raised Q2 guide 6% above consensus; HAMR ramp on track, supply tight through 2028
bullets.body: Seagate F1Q27 EPS $7.68 vs consensus $7.39, revenue $4.23B vs $4.11B; F2Q guide $9.00-9.40 EPS and $4.7-4.9B revenue both ~6% above consensus. HDD supply allocated through CY2028 with LTAs through 2030; HAMR expected ~50% of nearline exabytes by end-CY26. Citi trimmed PT to $1,050 (from $1,300) on peer multiple compression but reiterated Buy; JPM raised FY27/28 EPS to $40/$62.40.

bullets.title: ETSY: Clean Q3 beat-and-raise; active buyers return to growth for first time in 2 years
bullets.body: Q3 GMS +8.8% YoY to $2.65B (beat guidance of +4-6%); revenue $692.5M vs consensus $668.1M; adj. EBITDA margin 30.4% vs prior-year 25.4%. Q4 GMS guide $3.46-3.52B implies +5-7% YoY, 1pt above Street. FY GMS growth guidance raised to ~7% from mid-single-digits. $394.6M repurchased in Q3 with $2.2B authorization remaining. CFO Lanny Baker departs March 2027. JPM reiterates Overweight with $100 PT.

bullets.title: ENPH: -19% premarket; Q4 guide ~$240M midpoint misses $257-299M consensus, gross margin pressured
bullets.body: Enphase guided Q4 to $225-255M, well below consensus of $257-299M; baseline core demand running ~$200M/quarter per Opco. Gross margin under pressure from tariffs and battery storage mix. Opco and Morgan Stanley both downgraded to Perform/neutral. Mizuho cut 2027 revenue estimate by 14% to ~$1B. SEDG -8.6% in sympathy.

bullets.title: HOOD: -6.4% premarket; Q3 EPS miss on crypto weakness, but deposits and product velocity strong
bullets.body: Robinhood Q3 EPS $0.51 vs consensus $0.56; revenue $1.42B vs $1.44B expected; crypto market weakness cited. Adjusted EBITDA $808M beat consensus $778M. Total platform assets $395.9B (+18.9% YoY); Oct net deposits topped $13B MTD. Piper maintains Overweight citing 14 products generating >$100M revenue and record equities/options volumes. FY opex guidance narrowed positively to $2.675-2.75B.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye remains short at 38x P/E; smartphone shipments to fall 15% YoY in 2026-27
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags AAPL as a valuation bubble at 38x FY27 P/E with only single-digit growth expected; China share loss in non-premium segment accelerating and memory headwinds persist for 2+ quarters. Separately, global smartphone shipments expected -15% YoY in 2026 and 2027 with Chinese vendors -23% in 2027. The Zach AM note pegs FY27 EPS 13% below consensus on pull-forward iPhone demand fading. Stock up +27% YTD.

bullets.title: META/AVGO: AI financing overhangs cleared; META $97.5B raise, AVGO $63B custom-chip SPV
bullets.body: Meta announced a nearly $100B capital raise ($60B ATM deployment starting January); Broadcom announced a $63B custom-chip SPV; SpaceX closed a $40B GPU deal. These financing announcements drove semis +6.5% and memory +7.5% over Monday-Tuesday, with Nasdaq 100 posting back-to-back 1%+ gains for the first time in ~3 months. Goldman noted hedge fund net exposure near year lows heading in.

bullets.title: INTC: F3Q26 preview — street expects $16.5B revenue, $0.41 EPS; foundry momentum key catalyst
bullets.body: Consensus models $16.537B revenue, 41.7% gross margin, and $0.41 EPS for F3Q; F4Q consensus $17.124B/$0.44. Agentic AI demand expected to sustain server CPU growth; foundry sentiment improving with commitments from AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MSFT, and NVDA. 18A-P and 14A node timelines are primary investor focus. JPM buyside sentiment for INTC at +4/5 (near max long).

bullets.title: CLS: 3Q26 EPS $3.30 vs $2.96 consensus; 2027 revenue guided $40B (+90% YoY), FCF positive 2028
bullets.body: Celestica guided 2027 revenue to $40B vs Street $35.9B with 9% operating margin; flagged 2028 revenue meaningfully above 2027 and FCF positive in 2028 vs ~$3B outflow in 2027. JPM raised PT to $436, maintains Overweight. Stock lagging on FCF concerns near-term.

bullets.title: GLW: Optical-led beat in 3Q; 4Q guide above Street on GenAI enterprise demand
bullets.body: Corning optical sales +44% YoY on enterprise/GenAI demand doubling; Q4 guide $5.2-5.3B revenue and $0.96-$1.00 EPS both above Street. Maintains ~$1B 2027 photonics framework with 23% operating margin. JPM maintains Overweight.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Memory rally on SK Hynix blowout; supply sold out through 2029, shortage expected through 2030
bullets.body: SK Hynix Q3 operating profit +632% YoY with 79.7% OPM; DRAM and HBM effectively sold out through 2029 with LTAs covering >50% of 2027-2028 capacity. Announced ₩100tn (~$75.5B) shareholder return program. US sympathy: MU +3.5%, SNDK +4.1% premarket. NAND spot prices under pressure with 512Gb TLC -9.2% WoW.

bullets.title: NOW: ServiceNow cRPO estimate raised to 21% vs 20% guide; FY27 sub revenue ~17.3%
bullets.body: UBS and JPM both expect ServiceNow to beat cRPO growth guidance of 20% with estimates of 21%; FY27 subscription revenue growth estimated 17.3%. Reports today after close alongside MSFT and GOOGL.

bullets.title: ACN: CEO Julie Sweet purchases 12.2K shares at $235.16 — notable insider buy
bullets.body: Accenture Chair and CEO Julie Sweet purchased 12,200 shares of common stock at $235.16/share in a Form 4 filing, bringing her beneficial ownership to 48.9K shares. Meaningful insider purchase at current levels.

bullets.title: RCL: Q3 EPS $6.57 beats guide by ~$0.20; FY26 raised, Citi nudges PT to $364
bullets.body: Royal Caribbean Q3 adj. EPS $6.57 beat guidance of $6.26-6.36 and Street's $6.36 on stronger close-in Europe/Caribbean demand. Management raised FY26 EPS guidance to $17.85-17.95; Citi raised 2026E to $17.97, 2027E to $20.47, PT from $362 to $364. 3Q booking activity surged despite Middle East headlines.

bullets.title: CART: Downgraded to Hold at Gordon Haskett; PT cut to $62 on deal risk
bullets.body: Gordon Haskett downgraded Instacart to Hold from Buy and cut PT to $62 from $65, citing risks to a potential deal. No specific deal details provided.

bullets.title: TXN: DZ Bank upgrades to Hold from Sell; PT raised to $300 vs $308 current price
bullets.body: DZ Bank upgraded Texas Instruments to Hold from Sell, raising PT to $300 from $240. Current price $308.91 implies 3% downside to new target vs FactSet consensus of $338.96. Analyst Ingo Wermann.

bullets.title: INTU: Roth Capital launching Volume 13 QuickBooks adoption survey — watch for read-through
bullets.body: Roth Capital deploying survey targeting QuickBooks and QuickBooks Online users/non-users to measure adoption, satisfaction, and switching propensity among SMBs in US and UK. Results could provide leading indicator on Intuit's SMB retention and upsell trajectory.

bullets.title: AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL: Hyperscaler capex now 100% of OCF vs. 10-yr avg 40%; debt financing surging
bullets.body: Total hyperscaler capex reached ~$770B this year, equivalent to 100% of operating cash flow vs. the 10-year average of 40%. Debt financing rose from 9% of capex in FY24 to 32% over the last 12 months; Goldman expects hyperscaler debt issuance to rise 60% to ~$420B next year. AI-related issuers trading 115bps over Treasuries vs. 78bps for broader IG.

bullets.title: HOOD: Morgan Stanley notes 14 products >$100M revenue; Q3 net deposits $15.7B at 17% annualized pace
bullets.body: Despite the headline miss, Morgan Stanley highlights HOOD's product velocity (14 $100M+ revenue lines) and Q3 net deposits of $15.7B at a 17% annualized pace. Younger customers buying into selloffs supporting engagement metrics. October net deposits topped $13B MTD (~$7B ex-Trump Accounts).
